question: In human females, if the egg is not fertilised, the monthly shedding of the uterine lining is called which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Menstruation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Menstruation** is the natural, cyclic process in human females involving the shedding of the **endometrium** (the inner lining of the **uterus**).
 
• This process occurs specifically when the **ovum** (egg) released during the **ovulation** phase is **not fertilised** by a **sperm**.
 
• In the absence of **fertilisation**, the **corpus luteum** degenerates, leading to a sharp decline in the levels of **progesterone** and **estrogen** hormones.
 
• The lack of these hormones causes the **uterine lining** to break down, resulting in bleeding that exits the body through the **vagina**.
 
• A typical **menstrual flow** lasts for approximately **3 to 7 days**, and the entire **menstrual cycle** repeats roughly every **28 days**, although variations between **21 to 35 days** are considered normal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Menstrual Cycle Phases**:
 
 
• **Menstrual Phase**: The first stage where the **uterine lining** is shed.
 
• **Follicular Phase**: Starts on the first day of the period and ends with **ovulation**. The **pituitary gland** releases **Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)** to stimulate the **ovaries** to produce follicles.
 
• **Ovulation Phase**: Occurs around **day 14** of the cycle when a mature **egg** is released from the **ovary** into the **Fallopian tube**.
 
• **Luteal Phase**: The phase following ovulation where the **uterus** prepares for a potential **pregnancy** by thickening its lining.
 
 
 
• **Important Milestones**:
 
 
• **Menarche**: The very first occurrence of **menstruation** in a female, typically happening during **puberty** between the ages of **10 and 15**.
 
• **Menopause**: The biological stage marking the end of **menstrual cycles**, usually diagnosed after a woman has gone **12 months** without a period, typically occurring between the ages of **45 and 55**.
 
 
 
• **Clarification of Other Options**:
 
 
• **Maturation**: This refers to the biological process of **development**. In the reproductive context, it often refers to **oocyte maturation**, where an immature egg develops into a mature one within the **follicle**.
 
• **Fertilisation**: The process where a **sperm** cell fuses with an **egg** cell to form a **zygote**. This usually takes place in the **ampulla** of the **Fallopian tube**.
 
• **Maintenance**: In reproductive biology, this refers to the **maintenance of the endometrium** during **pregnancy**. If the egg is fertilised, the hormone **progesterone** prevents the lining from shedding to support the growing **embryo**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The cycle is regulated by a complex interplay of hormones from the **hypothalamus**, **pituitary gland**, and the **ovaries**.
 
• The **Endometrium** is highly vascularized (rich in blood vessels) to provide nutrients to a potential **fetus**; its shedding is what causes the **menstrual blood**.
 
• If **pregnancy** occurs, the **menstrual cycle** stops temporarily as the **placenta** begins producing **Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)** to maintain the **uterine lining**.
